maria (eng-ml): quick heads-up — saw a weird token-floor quality drift after enabling mixed-precision kernels on the new canary.
sam (infra): which model + config? h100 or l40s?
maria (eng-ml): atlas-13b, enabled fp8 kernels on h100 and l40s for the canary. AWQ/GPTQ int8 baseline looked fine. Issue shows up only on l40s when sequences >1024 tokens, punctuation tokens get substituted or dropped in ~0.7% of samples.
liam (runtime): do you have logs / numeric traces? sounds like a scale/handshake mismatch between kernel and quantization shim.
maria (eng-ml): pasted minimal repro and a small trace:
```
# repro
./run_infer --model atlas-13b --device l40s --seq_len 2048 --quant awq+fp8-kernel --prompt-file long_prefix.txt
# truncated trace
ATTN_KERNEL handshake: kernel_ver=1.3 fp8_enabled=1
qkv_scale_layer3: 1.2e-04 -> 3.4e-04 mismatch
attention_out[1023..1028]: "\u201c" -> "\u2019" (token id mismatch)
```
dev-ci-bot: canary deploy succeeded on h100-us-west-2 (canary id: c-2026-03-20-1)
maria (eng-ml): note: h100 canary didn't show the regression. only l40s. suggests kernel code path differs by device (tiling / block size). l40s fallback path to fp16 also has slightly different cache eviction timings.
sarah (product): how did this affect eval numbers? is it a perf vs quality trade?
maria (eng-ml): quick eval numbers vs baseline (full fp16): summarization rouge-L: -0.9 pts on l40s fp8 enabled; perplexity +1.2. h100 fp8 path: within noise (+0.1 rouge-L). not catastrophic but visible on long-prefix customer workloads.
liam (runtime): plausible root cause: mixed-precision accumulate + different kernel tiling yields subtle rounding bias after long KV reuse. also possible per-channel scale quantization combined with runqueue tiling leads to off-by-one accumulator order. I suspect activation re-scaling handshake isn't applied uniformly across runtime shards on l40s.
sam (infra): can we gate by sequence length? suggest disabling fp8 attention kernel when prefix_len > 768 on l40s, keep h100 enabled. cheap short-term mitigation.
maria (eng-ml): agreed. also need a deterministic unit test that reproduces token-floor: long-prefix generative sample with fixed seed and compare token stream to fp16 baseline.
liam (runtime): I'll add a deterministic reproducer in repo: tests/repro/long_prefix_token_floor.py and a runtime assert that compares top-1 token equality per-step for first N tokens. If mismatch rate > 0.3% we fail canary.
liam (runtime): small patch idea: apply per-op handshake barrier after qkv compute to ensure activation scaling factors are synchronized across shards before kv-write. cheap and might fix the ordering-induced rounding error.
sam (infra): runtime patch + canary gating sounds good. also add telemetry: per-token mismatch histogram and per-layer qkv_scale drift metric so we can quickly see regression during rollout.
maria (eng-ml): I'll run larger evals on our cust-eval harness (summ, convai, longform generation) once patch lands.
sarah (product): priority: medium-high — impacts long-tail customer flows. could be rollout blocker for l40s mixed-precision until mitigations.
liam (runtime): one more note — AWQ/GPTQ int8 paths didn't show the issue because they avoid that fp8 kernel handshake path entirely; good to mention in postmortem.
maria (eng-ml): opening issue now with steps and logs. PR incoming for the gating/telemetry. thanks.
sam (infra): thx — rolling back l40s fp8 canary for now (:thumbsup:). we'll keep h100 canary running and monitor.
maria (eng-ml): ack. i'll paste eval diffs in the issue when ready.
sarah (product): add a short blurb for release notes: "disabled mixed-precision kernel on L40S for long-prefix workloads pending numeric handshake fix" — i'll draft.
liam (runtime): will follow-up with a micro-benchmark showing where rounding accumulates across tiles.
maria (eng-ml): cool, thanks everyone."
